decision.title: 首期不提供生产 restore 工具与批准主体，固定受批准执行与宿主隔离合同
decision.summary: No production restore tool and no production approval role in phase one; production enter/resume DB replacement stays closed before Begin; ADR-0031 states the merged position with ADR-0030 that both production enter/install and the enter/resume DB replacement path stay closed, as different entry points rather than a narrowing. Only the existing restore-v1/verify-v1 software contract, deterministic test doubles and restore_unknown remain. The three HAN_RECOVERY_RESTORE_* keys keep no defaults and no inference. Any future production form must satisfy all six invariants and every release condition.
decision.approval_subject: Named deployment-side recovery approval role issues two independent records: backup source approval (SourceApprovalRef/Digest, artifact digest, source installation) and executable approval (absolute path, SHA256, owner/ACL, controlled read-only mount). The approver may not self-approve, may not be the executor or the run initiator, and may not be the tool/backup supplier approving its own artifact. No such role is appointed today.
decision.executor_subject: An independent non-interactive child process started by root, running under a dedicated execution identity distinct from root. Root does not execute in its place, does not enter a shell and does not replay; it keeps the deployment lock, Journal/keyring, Store binding/audit writes, recovery secret, Begin and final VerifyRestored. The execution identity gets only the read-only artifact fd, target connection via private stdin, minimal ENV allowlist and target DB network, and its target connection must be an independent DB role. The write boundary has two satisfiable layers: outside the replacement window that role privileges may not cover any write to Journal/keyring, deployment lock, Store authoritative binding or audit; inside the window the only writes to the target DB may come from the approved full-database artifact restore itself, the execution identity may not construct, inject or declare any authoritative binding and may not write Journal/keyring or the deployment lock, and root alone creates or verifies this run's running row and immutable binding through the same Store short transaction (design :3866); historical rows inside the artifact never count as this run's authority. Protected objects (Journal, keyring, deployment lock, Store authoritative binding, audit) form a checkable checklist fixed by the approval record and are only a post-restore cross-check item: full-database restore semantics are unchanged and no schema-level exclusion or root data migration is introduced. Identity switching and program launch must not be implemented through shell scripts, su or sudo wrappers; the concrete mechanism is fixed by the approval record and must be proven by isolation measurement at implementation time.
decision.host_isolation: Fixed argv direct exec of the single approved program with no shell and no extra argv; separate process group/session with full child-tree join/reap; no-follow stable fd/handle with pre/post fstat and path identity checks; minimal ENV allowlist with zero inherited business secrets or approval keys; no network beyond the target DB connection; any precheck failure rejects before Begin. POSIX is the only production candidate but remains closed in phase one; Windows production is unsupported and must return unsupported (exit code 2) before any state change, with test doubles and software trials only.
release_conditions: named recovery approval role appointed, with two independent approval records for backup source and executable (role, person, time, basis)
approved binary has verifiable SHA256, owner/ACL, controlled read-only mount, and update/rollback ownership

review_r02_rework.full_database_restore_consistency: Every write invariant holds simultaneously under full-database restore; nothing survives that only works for a partial restore, and no exception path was added. The tension between the execution identity being forbidden to write the Store and a full-database restore necessarily containing Store tables is resolved by separating historical rows inside the artifact (data being restored, never this run authority) from this run running row and immutable binding (created or verified only by root through the same Store short transaction per design :3866, with VerifyRestored still bound to the same artifact/target through the no-follow stable fd at :3870). This is not a silent relaxation: the identity still may not construct, inject or declare any authoritative binding and may not write Journal/keyring or the deployment lock.
